newsitem.title: USA: Analysts pleased with Westinghouse radio.
newsitem.headline: Analysts pleased with Westinghouse radio.

text.p: Wall Street analysts on Monday brushed off the third-quarter loss posted by Westinghouse Electric Corp and said they were suprisingly pleased by the company's radio operations, which posted a quarterly sales increase that outpaced the overall market.

Westinghouse posted a loss of $28 million, or $0.06 per share, an amount that included a $30 million charge for debt retirement. The company posted a net loss of $52 million, or $0.15 per share, in last year's third quarter.
"(The loss) is not what Westinghouse is all about," said Nick Heymann at NatWest Securities. "What this company is about is long-term strategy."
Excluding the charge, Westinghouse posted earnings of $0.00 per share on a continuing operations basis.
Wall Street's consensus estimate for the quarter was a loss of $0.01 per share. Shares of Westinghouse were up 1/8 to 17-1/2 in late-day trading.

Radio operations posted a 14 percent sales increase, outpacing the market. The company said higher sales, coupled with cost improvements drove a 52 percent increase in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA.)
"That 52 percent increase...that's good, heady stuff," Heymann said. "Radio did very well."
A Westinghouse spokesman said the company will close its $3.9 billion acquisition of radio giant Infinity Broadcasting by the end of the year.
The company also will announce its strategy for separating its broadcast and industrial businesses by year-end, he said.

Analysts said CBS, which Westinghouse bought last year for $5.4 billion, also did well in the third quarter. They said they were pleased with Westinghouse's integration of the network, which has been posting higher ratings in the 1996-1997 season compared with the prior season, spurred by a successful line-up of prime-time shows.
"The network did a shade better than we thought," said John Reidy at Smith Barney. "They're the only network that's up (in audience numbers) this year."
Compared with last year's third quarter, CBS sales were up about two percent, although EBITDA fell 12 percent.
Still, analysts said CBS has performed well in the ratings despite competition from programming, including the World Series and Monday Night Football.
"To have better ratings when you're up against the World Series and other things...it's like doing it with one hand tied behind your back," Heymann said.
"I think they have a good shot at being the No. 2 network for the year (behind NBC,") he said.
"In the first five weeks of the 96-97 season they gained or held their position. Everybody else has been flat."
The company spokesman said Westinghouse expects to sell $300 million to $500 million in assets, an amount that was previously announced.
The company already has sold a large portion of its industrial side and some analysts expect more of those assets to be sold, transforming Westinghouse into a pure media play.
